First, teachers elicit completion of their own utterance by strategically pausing to allow students to ‘fill in the blank’ (e.g., ‘It’s a ...’). Second, teachers use questions to elicit correct forms (e.g., ‘How do we say X in English?’). Third, teachers occasionally ask students to reformulate their utterance.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 A group activity in which learners have a free and relatively unstructured discussion on an assigned topic as a way of generating ideas.

cards.front: 〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 In teaching, a face-to-face conversation between a teacher and a student or a small group of students in which work being undertaken is discussed.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 In (  ) writing, the student’s writing is controlled by various means, such as by providing questions to be answered, sentences to be completed, or words or pictures to describe.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 A technique for teaching writing where the teacher provides detailed guidance in the form of questions, an outline, a model, or some other way of focusing and directing the students’ writing.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 In (  ) writing, the student’s writing is not controlled or limited in any way.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) reading is the practice of having a student read the same text over and over until their reading is fluent and error-free.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 The degree to which a message can be understood.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 The (  ) phonemes of English can be categorized as ‘vowel phonemes’ and ‘consonant phonemes.’
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 The segmental aspects of the English sound system – consonants and vowels – are often distinguished from the (  ) aspects – rhythm, stress, and intonation.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 The pronunciation of a syllable or word with more respiratory energy or muscular force than other syllables or words in the same utterance.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 In (  ) languages, the syllables are given equal length.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) has been called the music of speech. It is the meaningful use that speakers make of changes in their voice pitch.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 A unit of language that forms a syntactic or semantic unit.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 The term (  ) refers to restrictions on how words can be used together, such as which prepositions are used with particular verbs or which verbs and nouns are used together.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 A (  ) is a collection of actually occurring texts (either spoken or written), stored and accessed by means of computers, and useful for investigating language use.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 A (  ) is a list of words in a text, or in a corpus, along with each word’s immediate context.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 In (  ) learning, the learner is aware of what has been learned.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 The primary focus of classroom activity is on language forms rather than the meanings they convey.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) ( ) ( ) adheres to the principle that L2 teaching should essentially both involve and promote communication of meaning but that, at certain moments in the lesson when learners reveal a gap in their knowledge, the focus should switch from communicating messages to drawing the learners’ attention to formal aspects of the language, particularly its grammar.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) describes the way that learners become aware, or are made aware, of features of the language they are learning.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 By highlighting (e.g., making boldface) certain nonsalient grammatical forms in a reading passage, students’ attention will be drawn to them.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 Choosing texts in which a particular construction or structural contrast is especially frequent will enhance its saliency and thus might promote noticing.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 Rather than working on rule learning and rule application, (  ) ( ) activities push learners to attend to properties of language during activities where the structure is being used meaningfully. The goal of (  ) ( ) instruction is to encourage learners to make better form-meaning connections than they would if left to their own devices.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 A (  ) task consists of a short text, designed to contain multiple exemplars of a specific linguistic feature. This is read twice to students at normal speed while they take notes. The students then work collaboratively in groups to reconstruct the text from their notes.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) is the repetition of the accented vowel sound and any succeeding consonant sounds. (  ) is frequently used in children’s songs, poems or stories, especially at the end of lines.

cards.front: 〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 A (  ) question is one that is framed with only one acceptable answer in mind.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 Teaching consists of (  ), that is, regular procedures that impart a sense of structure, rhythm and flow to the class. Some (  ) are management-oriented, such as checking attendance or re-organizing seating into groups. Others are teaching-oriented, such as checking homework, drilling, brainstorming vocabulary, or playing a game like ‘twenty questions.’

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) refers to the use of clear illustrations and examples for learners. (  ) activities, in their basic conception, require a teacher to demonstrate or show the task that the students will be asked to produce in the future.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) ensures that tests are feasible given time, resources, and classroom constraints.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 If your aim in a test is to tap global competence in a language, then you are, in conventional terminology, testing (  ).

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 Certain proficiency tests and diagnostic tests can act in the role of (  ) tests, whose purpose is to place a student into an appropriate level or section of a language curriculum or school.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 An (  ) test is related directly to classroom lessons, units, or even a total curriculum. (  ) tests are limited to particular material covered in a curriculum within a particular time frame, and are offered after a course has covered the objectives in question.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) assessment refers to evaluating students in the process of “forming” their competencies and skills with the goal of helping them to continue that growth process.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) assessment aims to measure, or summarize, what a student has grasped and typically occurs at the end of a course or unit of instruction.
〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 (  ) testing involves the test-taker in actually performing the target task.

〔3.영어 · 강사 질문〕 Teachers commonly observe learners’ performance in the classroom on a day-to-day basis and follow this up with some kind of diagnostic feedback, either verbal or written, which alerts the learner to his or her strengths or weaknesses.
